oneLiner: A launch monopoly and Starlink cash engine that has become, by revenue, mostly a GPU landlord (Super Intelligence was over half of Q3 2026 sales). The market is betting that contracted AI compute keeps scaling toward the Q1 2027 guide and beyond, and that the buildout can be funded without swamping shareholders.
thesis: The revenue step change is contracted, not hoped for. Q1 2027 revenue was guided to $33-37B against a ~$22.2B LSEG consensus, and Anthropic's S-1 discloses up to $120.5B of SpaceX compute commitments into 2029, about $3.1B a month once capacity is fully delivered in December 2026.

Compute economics are better than a typical neocloud. SI segment adjusted EBITDA was $5.0B on $7.6B of Q3 2026 revenue (~66%), on pricing reported above $50 per watt a year; SpaceX controls power, sites and its own models (Grok, Cursor), not just racks.

Starlink is still compounding underneath. Connectivity operating income grew 99% YoY in Q3 2026 while enterprise and government revenue grew 91%; the 800 MHz spectrum deal (signed Oct 8, closing H1 2027) opens a direct-to-phone business.

Starship moved from test article to payload carrier. Flight 14 was the first orbital and first revenue-generating Starship flight, carrying 26 Starlink V3 satellites (~10x the downlink capacity of a Falcon 9 Starlink launch), which lowers the cost of every future Starlink and Starship-based payload.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30, 2026; reported Oct 20, 2026)
points: Revenue $14.58B, +161% YoY, vs ~$12.6-12.7B consensus; SI $7.56B (+830% YoY), Connectivity $5.25B (+69%), Space $1.77B (+6%).
Income from operations $2.79B (Q2: -$143M); net income $4.40B, diluted EPS $0.35 vs ~$0.10 consensus, helped by $1.03B other income and a $390M tax benefit.
Adjusted EBITDA $8.81B (+306% YoY); $2.36B of share-based compensation, of which $1.22B tied to the Cursor acquisition.
Capex $19.59B, of which $16.44B SI; nameplate compute 1.7 GW (1.4 GW at Jun 30).
Starlink consumer subscribers 13.6M (+1.6M QoQ); consumer ARPU $69/month (Q2 $66, Q3 2025 $83). Launches 35 (Q3 2025: 44).

segments: Super Intelligence (~52% of Q3 2026 revenue): cloud compute (Colossus I and II, ~$7.0B solutions and infrastructure revenue), Grok models and Grok Bot, advertising ($538M) and Cursor (acquired Aug 14, 2026, $608M of revenue through Sep 30).

Connectivity (~36%): Starlink consumer ($3.12B) plus enterprise and government ($2.13B), ~11,100 satellites in orbit (new definition includes ~400 de-orbit-approved), 3,800+ aircraft; segment operating income $2.37B.

Space (~12%): Falcon launch ($1.13B of launch services revenue) and development contracts; Q3 pipeline added 3 NASA ISS crew missions, 18 National Security Space Launch missions and a Starship lunar payload contract. Segment roughly break-even (-$7M) after Starship R&D.
competitive: CoreWeave, Nebius and the hyperscalers: SI competes for the same frontier-lab compute budgets; Anthropic's S-1 also names Microsoft, Nscale and Lambda as GPU providers, so SpaceX is one supplier of several, not a sole source.
Amazon Kuiper and AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): broadband and direct-to-device rivals; the 800 MHz spectrum purchase is SpaceX's answer to carrier-partnered D2D.
Rocket Lab (RKLB), ULA and Blue Origin: launch challengers years behind on reusable cadence; national-security launch awards remain politically contestable.
OpenAI, Google and Anthropic on models: Grok and Cursor put SpaceX in direct competition with its own largest compute customers.
moat: Two deep moats and one rented one. Reusable launch and the Starlink constellation it alone can deploy cheaply are structural advantages no rival matches this decade, now extended by an operational Starship. The SI business is built on purchased Nvidia GPUs and contracts that become cancellable on 90 days' notice in 2027; its edge is speed of power and site build-out, which is real but replicable with enough capital.
risks: Capex runs ahead of cash. Trailing capex is ~1.7x revenue; Q4 2026 capex is guided to $35-40B against ~$90B of cash and marketable securities at Sep 30, and Musk targets at least 10 GW of added compute in 2027, which at reported build costs implies external financing.

Customer concentration with an exit door. Anthropic alone could be ~$37B a year at full delivery, and its initial non-cancelable periods end in January and March 2027, after which either side can cancel on 90 days' notice; Google ($920M a month) is the other anchor.

Earnings quality and dilution. Q3 net income exceeded operating income by $1.6B on other income and a tax benefit; Cursor brings $23.4B of post-acquisition stock compensation over about three years, and Q4 gross margin was guided back to Q2 levels after a ~3-point one-time tariff refund in Connectivity.

Governance and the Tesla question. SpaceX and Tesla boards formed special committees (Oct 20, 2026) to examine a combination; Musk is recused, but a deal would set an exchange ratio between two Musk-controlled companies and could add billions of shares.

Supply overhang. Staged lockup releases continue through the final 180-day expiry around Dec 8, 2026 (date unverified), and Musk's stake unlocks June 2027; S&P 500 eligibility is reported to require one year of seasoning.
catalysts: Dec 3, 2026: Tesla annual meeting; Barclays suggests merger terms could surface before it (debate 3).
Dec 2026: Anthropic expects full contracted capacity delivered (~$3.1B a month); Q4 exit compute target 2.5-3 GW (debate 1).
Jan and Mar 2027: Anthropic's initial non-cancelable periods end (debate 1).
Q4 2026 report, ~late Jan 2027 (date unconfirmed): FY2027 capex plan and how it is funded (debate 2).
H1 2027: 800 MHz spectrum deal closes; Starship Flight 15 and the next V3 deployments (dates unconfirmed).

valPresets.note: Revenue mode: quarterly capex ($19.6B in Q3 2026, $35-40B guided for Q4) swamps EBITDA, so near-term FCF is deeply negative and margin-based modes mislead. The CAGR presets are 7-year averages from the FY2026 base and sit below the Q1 2027 guide on purpose: they price durable growth after the compute ramp, not the ramp itself.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Oct 20). Revenue $14.58B, +161% YoY and nearly double Q2, beating ~$12.6-12.7B consensus by about $2B. The mix flipped: Super Intelligence revenue of $7.56B now exceeds Connectivity, driven by newly activated cloud agreements, Cursor and Grok. Income from operations turned positive at $2.79B, and net income of $4.40B ($0.35 diluted) included $1.03B of other income and a $390M tax benefit. Connectivity operating income was $2.37B; Space was break-even as Starship R&D absorbed launch profit. Capex was $19.59B (SI $16.44B), and cash plus marketable securities ended at $89.9B. Starlink consumer additions of 1.6M came mostly from developed markets, with ARPU up sequentially but well below a year ago as cheaper plans and markets dominate the base.
guidanceProse: SpaceX gave its first explicit outlook on the Oct 20 call: Q1 2027 revenue of $33-37B, more than double Q3 and roughly $13B above consensus, plus Q4 2026 capex of $35-40B and nameplate compute of 2.5-3 GW by year-end. Q4 gross margin is guided back toward Q2 levels. Musk added at least 10 GW of incremental compute in 2027 (a small chance of 20 GW) and floated $500B-1T of annual recurring revenue by end-2027; that is his aspiration, not company guidance. Reported backlog rose to $63B from $47.5B (per call coverage, unverified against filings). No FY2027 revenue or capex guide yet.

verdict.stance: Neutral - the guide is real, the bill is not yet priced
verdict.summary: Q3 changed the question. SpaceX is no longer asking investors to pay for Starship optionality; it is asking them to underwrite a compute business that could be most of a ~$140B annualized revenue run-rate by Q1 2027. Our probability-weighted value sits modestly below the current price: the base case gives full credit to a ~$190B FY2027 but pays a compute-like 9x sales for it, because the dominant customer can walk on 90 days' notice from early 2027 and 10 GW of 2027 build-out cannot be funded from cash on hand. Two things would move us to Positive: Anthropic and Google extending past their non-cancelable periods, and a FY2027 capex plan funded mostly by debt and operating cash rather than new shares. A dilutive Tesla deal or an Anthropic step-down would move us to Cautious.
wtb: Q1 2027 revenue lands inside the $33-37B guide, and FY2027 reaches ~$190B or more, which needs compute capacity near 5 GW+ by mid-2027.
Anthropic does not cancel or reprice after its non-cancelable periods end in January and March 2027; SI revenue keeps rising sequentially through Q2 2027.
FY2027 capex is funded with less than ~3% net share dilution, and cash plus securities stay above ~$40B at end-2027.
The market keeps paying at least ~9x sales at end-2027, which implies Starlink plus launch are valued as franchises and compute EBITDA margins stay near 55-65%.

bear.why: Anthropic scales back after March 2027 and compute pricing resets toward neocloud levels; revenue stalls near the Q1 2027 run-rate (~$120B for the year). Funding the build-out needs equity, and the market values the company like a leveraged GPU landlord with a satellite business attached.

base.why: Q1 2027 lands mid-guide and capacity ramps toward 5-6 GW by year-end, so quarterly revenue steps from ~$35B to ~$60B; compute dominates the mix with ~55-60% EBITDA margins. The multiple (~16x EBITDA) is a blend: high for Starlink and launch, compute-like for SI, because contract renewals beyond 2027 are not yet visible.

bull.why: The 10 GW+ 2027 plan largely lands, more frontier labs sign beyond Anthropic and Google, and Starlink Mobile adds a new growth leg. Contracts extend into 2029-2030, earning a multiple that treats compute as a utility-like contracted stream rather than spot rental.

scenarioModel.note: Value per share = (FY2027 revenue x EV/Sales + ~$60B net cash) / ~13.6B shares (market cap / price, which includes Cursor and post-IPO issuance; Q3 diluted weighted shares were 12.48B). Bear $120B x 6 = ~$57; base $190B x 9 = ~$130; bull $260B x 12 = ~$234; weighted ~$129. Net cash is the current figure and will shrink with Q4 capex; new equity would lower all three. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Is the compute revenue durable once the contracts become cancellable?
debates.bull: Anthropic signed or amended several agreements between May and October 2026 and expects all capacity delivered in December 2026; frontier labs are capacity-constrained, so renewal on similar terms is the default.
debates.bear: From early 2027 either side can cancel on 90 days' notice, Anthropic lists three other GPU providers, and SpaceX's own Grok and Cursor compete with its tenants. A ~$37B-a-year customer with an exit door is not a moat.
debates.view: This sets the multiple more than any other variable: we price 9x in the base case precisely because renewal is not yet visible. A clean extension through 2029 is worth moving the base multiple toward the bull case.

signpost.metric: Anthropic contract status after its non-cancelable periods; Q1 2027 SI revenue vs Q4 2026
signpost.threshold: bullish if extended or upsized; bearish if any notice of cancellation or SI revenue falls QoQ

debates.bull: Compute pricing above $50 per watt a year with ~66% SI EBITDA margins implies payback in roughly two years; operating cash flow ($9.6B in Q3) is ramping with revenue, and the balance sheet holds ~$90B of cash and securities.
debates.bear: Trailing capex is ~1.7x revenue and free cash flow was -$40B over the last four quarters before Q4's $35-40B; the reverse DCF already needs ~83% annual revenue growth for seven years, so any equity raise lands on a price that assumes the plan succeeds.
debates.view: The growth is fundable only if lenders treat the contracts as collateral. The mix of debt, vendor financing and new shares in the FY2027 plan matters more than the capex number itself.

signpost.metric: FY2027 capex guide and funding mix (debt / operating cash vs new equity)
signpost.threshold: net dilution above 3% of shares or cash plus securities below $40B = bearish

debates.q: Does a Tesla combination create or transfer value for SPCX holders?
debates.bull: A combined company gets one capital pool for compute, robotics and energy, Tesla's cash flow and buyers, and removes the related-party friction between the two.
debates.bear: An all-stock deal at a rich exchange ratio would add billions of shares to an already capex-hungry company; it needs a majority of all Tesla shares, so terms may have to favour Tesla holders.
debates.view: Neutral until terms exist. A deal priced near current relative values is roughly a wash per share; we would move to Cautious if it is paid with SPCX stock at a premium plus new financing needs.

signpost.metric: Announced exchange ratio and implied premium to Tesla
signpost.threshold: premium above ~20% to Tesla holders paid in SPCX stock = bearish
signpost.when: Before Tesla's annual meeting, Dec 3, 2026 (timing per Barclays, unverified)
